subject: Spiders
hook: SPIDERS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The legendary 'giant spider' Megarachne servinei, once thought to be a 1.8-foot-wide monster, was actually a relatively small sea scorpion.
angle_support: Megarachne servinei from the late Carboniferous was once thought to be a giant mygalomorph spider and, with its body length of 54 cm (1.8 ft) and leg span of above 50 cm (20 in), the largest known spider ever to have lived on Earth, but subsequent examination revealed that it was actually a relatively small sea scorpion.
title: The ‘Giant Spider’ Was Actually a Tiny Sea Scorpion
description: Megarachne was once celebrated as the biggest spider ever, spanning nearly two feet. New research shows it was a far smaller sea scorpion from the Carboniferous era, rewriting its legend.
narration: SPIDERS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture Megarachne as a monstrous 1.8‑foot‑wide spider, the biggest ever. In reality, it wasn’t a spider at all but a modest sea scorpion that lived in ancient seas. Megarachne servinei measured 54 cm in body length with a leg span over 50 cm, earning the title of the largest known spider, but detailed study later identified it as a modest‑sized sea scorpion from the Carboniferous period. So the feared giant spider was really an ancient sea scorpion.
